title:
Predicting Falcon 9
first-stage landing outcomes
bullets: A reproducible data-science study of historical SpaceX launches
Collection • Wrangling • SQL • Visual analytics • Machine learning
Presenter: Hrant Ohannes Kasparian
subtitle: DATA SCIENCE  /  HISTORICAL COHORTS 2010–2020
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Strong signals; limited evidence for deployment
bullets: 90-launch modeling cohort: 60 successful landings (66.7%).
Methods: archived API data, Pandas cleaning, SQLite, six EDA plots, Folium, Dash and four tuned classifiers.
All four models score 15/18 = 83.3% test accuracy; the tree leads 10-fold CV at 87.7%.
Critical risks: only 18 test launches, false-positive landings and possible time/booster leakage.
Wikipedia retrieval is blocked; scraping code is supplied, not a fabricated scraped result.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Business question: can a first stage be recovered?
bullets: Objective: predict the course-defined binary landing class from launch and booster attributes.
Why it matters: recovery can support reuse planning; this study does not estimate actual launch costs or savings.
Success is a first-stage outcome, not payload-delivery mission success.
Decision framing: avoid overconfidence when predicting a successful landing.
Scope: historical educational snapshots, not current SpaceX performance.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Three cohorts—not one interchangeable dataset
bullets: Labels and launch-site spellings differ across cohorts. Never mix their denominators.
table: Interactive visual analytics / older launch subset

title: Archived API response → enriched launch table
bullets: GET /v4/launches/past → parse JSON → filter Falcon 9.
Resolve rocket, launchpad, payload and core IDs through their v4 endpoints.
Select single-payload/single-core launches; apply the lab cutoff; flatten launch metadata.
Archived response: 107 launches, including 99 Falcon 9, 5 Falcon 1 and 3 Falcon Heavy.
Live endpoint returned HTTP 522 here; modeling uses the frozen course CSVs, not a claimed live rebuild.
source: Source: course API_call_spacex_api.json; API schema: github.com/r-spacex/SpaceX-API. GitHub: github.com/hrantk28-stack/SpaceX-Falcon9-Capstone

title: Request → inspect → parse → normalize → validate
bullets: Task 1: request the June 9, 2021 Wikipedia revision (oldid 1027686922), check status and create BeautifulSoup.
Task 2: find launch tables and clean <th> names; remove footnotes and normalize whitespace.
Task 3: parse numbered launch rows; handle rowspans; build a DataFrame and export CSV.
Expected fields: flight, date/time, booster, site, payload, mass, orbit, customer and both outcomes.
Verified limit: HTTP 403 prevented extraction. No scraped row count is asserted.
source: Source: attached web-scraping notebook; collection.py provides all three task solutions. GitHub: github.com/hrantk28-stack/SpaceX-Falcon9-Capstone

title: Define the target before interpreting “success”
bullets: Inspect shape, dtypes, missingness and categorical values before transforming.
Class 0: False Ocean, False RTLS, False ASDS, None ASDS and None None.
Class 1: True ASDS, True RTLS and True Ocean → 60/90 successes.
True Ocean (5 records) counts as class 1 in the lab but does not prove recoverability or reuse.
26/90 LandingPad values are missing (28.9%); missing pad dummies are all zero. Payload is already imputed in the course CSV.
source: Source: dataset_part_1.csv and dataset_part_2.csv; analyze.py. GitHub: github.com/hrantk28-stack/SpaceX-Falcon9-Capstone

bullets: Outcome counts: True ASDS 41; None None 19; True RTLS 14; False ASDS 6; True Ocean 5; False Ocean 2; None ASDS 2; False RTLS 1.
Wrangling Task 2 excludes GTO as instructed: 63 launches remain. EDA/ML retain the full 90-launch cohort.

title: Six views answer six different questions
bullets: Flight number × site: inspect experience and site mix.
Payload × site: compare payload operating ranges.
Orbit bars: compare average class, with sample-size labels.
Flight number × orbit and payload × orbit: reveal mixed mission contexts.
Yearly line: summarize changing performance; use year-specific denominators.
Association only: experience, vehicle generation, payload and site are confounded.
source: Source: dataset_part_2.csv; analyze.py and completed_answers.ipynb. GitHub: github.com/hrantk28-stack/SpaceX-Falcon9-Capstone

title: Later flights show more successful outcomes
bullets: CCAFS dominates the cohort (55/90) and includes the earliest unsuccessful landings.
KSC begins later in the sequence, making site and experience difficult to separate.
KSC: 17/22 successes; VAFB: 10/13. Their similar rates have different sample sizes.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Payload envelopes vary by launch site
bullets: VAFB maximum observed payload: 9,600 kg—no launches above 10,000 kg in this cohort.
CCAFS and KSC each reach 15,600 kg.
Some masses are course-imputed; do not interpret every plotted value as a measured payload.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Perfect rates are often small-sample artifacts
bullets: SSO: 5/5 = 100%. ES-L1, GEO and HEO each have only one successful observation.
SO: 0/1. Neither 0% nor 100% from one launch is a robust forecast.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Flight sequence and orbit context interact
bullets: LEO transitions from early class 0 observations toward later successes.
GTO contains both classes across the flight sequence; it is not cleanly separable.
FlightNumber is also a time proxy—not a causal measure of learning.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Payload alone does not separate landing classes
bullets: GTO successes and failures overlap strongly in payload mass.
VLEO launches carry 13,620–15,600 kg and achieve 12/14 successes.
Mission energy, booster generation and landing plan matter; mass alone is insufficient.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: The annual trend improves—but not monotonically
bullets: 2020: 16/19 = 84.2%. The template’s “kept increasing” claim is contradicted by the data.
No 2011 observations; do not interpolate a measured rate.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: 90 observations → 83 numeric predictors
bullets: Tasks 7–8: one-hot encode Orbit, LaunchSite, LandingPad, Serial, GridFins, Reused and Legs.
Retain FlightNumber, PayloadMass, Flights, Block and ReusedCount.
Cast every feature to float64; rebuilt values match the provided 90 × 83 model matrix.
Exclude Class and Outcome from predictors. Serial identifiers and repeated boosters still create leakage risks.
For production: audit when Flights/ReusedCount were measured; remove any post-launch information.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: SQLite audit: ten queries, one explicit contract
bullets: Load the 101-row CSV into SPACEXTBL and trim string whitespace.
Use DISTINCT, LIKE, SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX, GROUP BY, a subquery and date filtering.
Task 4 interprets “F9 v1.1” as a version family: LIKE 'F9 v1.1%'.
Task 7 groups all Success-prefixed mission labels; landing outcome is a different field.
Complete SQL and row-level outputs are included in the detailed report.
source: Source: Spacex.csv; sql_answers.sql. GitHub: github.com/hrantk28-stack/SpaceX-Falcon9-Capstone

bullets: Task 6: drone-ship successes, 4,000 < mass < 6,000 kg: F9 FT B1022, B1026, B1021.2 and B1031.2.

title: Folium explains location; Dash explains filters
bullets: Folium: site circles, red/green launch markers, marker clusters, MousePosition and distance lines.
Dash: searchable site dropdown, all-site success-share pie and selected-site outcome pie.
A 0–10,000 kg RangeSlider filters payload scatter; booster category is encoded by color.

title: Launch sites are coastal, not on the Equator
bullets: The course locations span about 28.6°N to 34.6°N: none are equatorial.
Florida sites appear on the Atlantic side; VAFB is on the Pacific side.
Coastal geography is consistent with downrange ocean corridors; it does not establish site-selection causality.
Coordinates and site labels are used exactly as supplied, not independently surveyed.
source: Source: course geo CSV; Folium screenshot; basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors.

title: Clustered launch records reveal site-level outcomes
bullets: 56 launch markers: green = class 1, red = class 0; coincident markers cluster.
KSC LC-39A: 10/13 successful; CCAFS LC-40: 7/26.
VAFB SLC-4E: 4/10; CCAFS SLC-40: 3/7.
CCAFS LC-40 and SLC-40 are retained as distinct course labels; they refer to the same named complex across eras.
source: Source: geo CSV and launch_map.html; basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors.

title: Proximity analysis: calculated, not surveyed
bullets: From course CCAFS LC-40 point: selected coastline point ≈0.58 km; Titusville reference center ≈23.16 km.
Illustrative road-corridor point ≈0.55 km; rail-corridor point ≈1.31 km. Feature identity is unverified.
Distances are haversine point-to-point, not road routes or validated nearest-feature distances.
Conclusion: coastal access and city separation are plausible; nearest railway/highway claims remain unverified.
source: Source: course coordinates + explicitly illustrative reference points; OpenStreetMap basemap. See report caveats.

bullets: All-site view counts only successful launches for the pie.
Selected-site view compares class 1 with class 0.

Both callbacks were browser-tested; this is a screenshot of the running local app.

title: KSC leads both success count and success rate
bullets: Q1: KSC LC-39A has 10 successes—the largest count.
Q2: KSC LC-39A also has the highest rate: 10/13 = 76.9%.
All-site pie: KSC contributes 10/24 = 41.7% of successes. This is not its site success rate.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Payload-bin rankings depend on the definition
bullets: Using fixed 1,000 kg bins, highest observed rate: (3,000, 4,000] kg, 8/11 = 72.7%.
Lowest nonempty bin: (6,000, 7,000] kg, 0/4 = 0%.
Exclude empty bins from ranking; (7,000, 9,000] kg has no observations.
Zero payload values may mean unknown mass. Binning is descriptive, not a recommended operating threshold.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: B5 wins on rate—but has only one observation
bullets: FT is strongest among categories with at least five observations in this sample.
Later booster versions are confounded with calendar time, mission mix and landing capability.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: One holdout, four tuned classifiers, two protocols
bullets: Tasks 1–3: Y = Class.to_numpy(); 80/20 split, random_state=2 → 72 train and 18 test.
Tasks 4–11: tune logistic regression, SVM, decision tree and KNN using 10-fold CV.
Course reproduction: standardize before split, as instructed. This leaks preprocessing information.
Preferred sensitivity run: StandardScaler inside a Pipeline, fitted separately within each CV fold.
Compatibility fix: deprecated tree max_features=auto is equivalent to sqrt for classification; set seed=2.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Decision tree leads CV; all models tie on the test
bullets: Pipeline protocol. Every model: precision 0.800 and recall 1.000 for class 1.
Majority-class baseline on test: 12/18 = 66.7%. Model gain = 16.7 percentage points.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Rank using CV—not a tied test score
bullets: Decision tree CV = 87.7%; KNN = 84.8%; logistic regression = 84.6%; SVM = 82.1%.
Course reproduction CV: tree 87.7%, SVM 84.8%, KNN 84.8%, logistic regression 84.6%.
Moving scaling inside folds changes SVM tuning, not the 83.3% test result.
Select the tree as the provisional CV leader; do not claim proven test superiority.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: False positives are the unresolved operational risk
bullets: Every model returns the same test matrix: TN=3, FP=3, FN=0, TP=12.
Three of six actual class 0 launches are predicted successful: false-positive rate = 50%.
Recall of successful landings is 100%, but failure-class recall is only 50%.
18 test records are too few for deployment assurance; one changed prediction moves accuracy by 5.6 points.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Provisional choice: a constrained decision tree
bullets: Best pipeline settings: criterion=gini, splitter=best, max_depth=8, max_features=sqrt.
min_samples_leaf=2, min_samples_split=10, random_state=2.
Highest CV score: 0.8768. Test score: 0.8333. A ranking, not proof of generalization.
Next validation: time-ordered holdout and booster-group separation; remove serial IDs and audit prelaunch availability.
Use calibrated probabilities and a false-positive-aware threshold before any operational decision.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.

title: Separate prediction, recoverability and business value
bullets: Landing performance improves broadly over time, but annual setbacks and mission mix matter.
KSC leads observed site rates; small samples prevent causal or universal rankings.
Four classifiers beat a simple baseline, yet half of test failures are missed.
Creative extension: two-stage modeling—first landing attempt/strategy, then success conditional on attempt.
A business case also needs recovery condition, turnaround time and refurbishment cost—none are available here.
source: IBM Skills Network course datasets; independently recomputed for this project.
